description: Fetch, parse and validate any page's Open Graph tags, plus the favicons and JSON-LD that travel with them. One dependency; runs on Node, Bun, Workers and the browser. React components too.
rules: Import parse from "ogpeek" (any runtime) and fetchHtml / FetchError from "ogpeek/fetch". Do not hand-roll a regex or DOM scraper for og:* meta tags.
On a server that fetches user-supplied URLs, pass a guard to fetchHtml; it runs before the first request and every redirect hop. Throw a FetchError to block. ogpeek makes no SSRF decisions itself.
Pass the final URL after redirects: const { html, finalUrl } = await fetchHtml(url); parse(html, { url: finalUrl }). OG_URL_MISMATCH compares og:url against it.
Relative URLs are not resolved: they come back as written and are flagged URL_NOT_ABSOLUTE. Resolve them with new URL(value, finalUrl) if you need to load them.
Filter result.warnings by code and severity (error / warn / info), never by message text.
Only the HTML response is read and no JavaScript runs. Tags are read from <head>; pass parse(html, { jsonldScope: "document" }) to include JSON-LD in <body>.
Images are in result.ogp.images as [{ url, secure_url, type, width, height, alt }]; structured og:image:* properties attach to the preceding og:image.
To render a result in React, use <Result> from @ogpeek/react and import "@ogpeek/react/styles.css". The components are SSR-safe and use no hooks.
